newsitem.title: FINLAND: T.HALONEN UP ON MILK WHEY FINDING - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: T.HALONEN UP ON MILK WHEY FINDING - PAPER.

text.p: Finnish food technology group Tuomo Halonen Oy's new process, which enables milk whey to be used as a raw material of baby food, has boosted its share price this year, business daily Kauppalehti reported on Monday.

"Investors have already realised that the baby food process is the most significant product group in the company's history," Kauppalehti quoted Tuomo Halonen managing director Jarmo Halonen as saying.
Tuomo Halonen's share price has more than tripled this year. It closed at 23.00 markka on December 3 after a calendar year low of 9.00 markka set on January 24.
Milk whey has so far been a largely useless sideproduct of the cheese industry.
There are nine kg of milk whey for each kg of cheese produced, Kauppalehti said.
Tuomo Halonen, which is due to be renamed Elecster from the beginning of 1997, is currently building a baby food plant in Russia worth tens of millions of markka, the paper said.
